reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
name: ASITN/SIR Collateral Flow Grade

version.label: ASITN/SIR collateral flow grading (Higashida et al. 2003)
version.detail: Grades 0–4 on catheter angiography. CT-angiography collateral scores (e.g. Tan, Maas, Menon) are different systems.

purpose: Grades angiographic collateral flow to the ischaemic territory.
intendedPopulation: Patients with acute arterial occlusion undergoing catheter angiography.

options.label: No collaterals
options.detail: No collaterals visible to the ischaemic site.

options.label: Slow, peripheral
options.detail: Slow collaterals to the periphery of the ischaemic site, with part of the defect persisting.

options.label: Rapid, peripheral
options.detail: Rapid collaterals to the periphery of the ischaemic site, with part of the defect persisting.

options.label: Slow but complete
options.detail: Collaterals give slow but complete filling of the ischaemic bed by the late venous phase.

options.label: Complete and rapid
options.detail: Complete and rapid retrograde collateral flow to the entire ischaemic territory, at this assessment.

resultStates.label: No collaterals
resultStates.summary: No collaterals visible to the ischaemic site.
resultStates.detail: Assess with the full imaging picture; poor collaterals are associated with larger infarcts.

resultStates.label: Slow, peripheral
resultStates.summary: Slow collaterals to the periphery of the ischaemic site, with part of the defect persisting.

resultStates.label: Rapid, peripheral
resultStates.summary: Rapid collaterals to the periphery of the ischaemic site, with part of the defect persisting.

resultStates.label: Slow but complete
resultStates.summary: Collaterals give slow but complete filling of the ischaemic bed by the late venous phase.

resultStates.label: Complete and rapid
resultStates.summary: Complete and rapid retrograde collateral flow to the entire ischaemic territory, at this assessment.
resultStates.detail: Good collaterals are associated with smaller infarcts but do not guarantee outcome.

clinicalContext.text: Collateral status modifies how quickly the ischaemic core grows.

clinicalInsights.text: Grade on late arterial and venous phases; collaterals fill late.

limitations.text: Requires catheter angiography of the collateral supply; often incompletely assessed during thrombectomy.

confounders.effect: Collateral sources may not be opacified.

guideSections.what: A five-level angiographic grade of collateral flow (0–4).
guideSections.whenToUse: Angiographic assessment in acute ischaemic stroke.
guideSections.howToPerform: Assess the rate and extent of collateral filling of the ischaemic territory through the venous phase; choose the grade.
guideSections.clinicalContext: One imaging marker among core, perfusion and timing.

sources.citation: Higashida RT, Furlan AJ, Roberts H, et al. Trial design and reporting standards for intra-arterial cerebral thrombolysis for acute ischemic stroke. Stroke. 2003;34(8):e109-e137.
